items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (createPersisterRestoreResult, normalizeInfiniteQueryData), but the restore helpers are mixed into query.ts with no doc comments. The consumed-flag mechanism (PERSISTER_RESTORE_CONSUMED_SYMBOL via Object.defineProperty) and the pageParams fallback logic have no explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Helpers sit in query.ts instead of a dedicated persister.ts. Mutable 'consumed' marking via defineProperty is a side channel. Internal helpers are exported publicly (isPersisterRestoreResultConsumed, normalizeInfiniteQueryData). The vue useBaseQuery.ts adapter was changed although adapters should need no changes. About 1364 insertions.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult passes `state: input.state` through without normalising counts, timestamps or status. normalizeInfiniteQueryData uses `(data as any).pages` duck typing, and markPersisterRestoreResultConsumed takes PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: Exported from query-core with a non-enumerable Symbol.for marker, but a global-registry symbol can be forged. Tests show no onSuccess/onSettled calls and fetchStatus 'fetching' becomes 'idle'. The bulk-path code is elided, so I can't confirm it shares one helper with the per-query restore. F2P 8/8.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: New exports are additive and P2P 42/42 pass. However, vue-query/src/useBaseQuery.ts gains a new `else { unsubscribe = observer.subscribe(...) }` branch, which changes adapter subscription behaviour for all queries, not only persisted ones. Persist-client internals are mostly elided.
